feedbackActionPlan.summary: Keep or add a deflection preference field in the custom shaft order flow so customers can describe the playability they want before spec review, without promising an exact measured deflection result.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers who care about cue-ball deflection when using side spin can communicate whether they want low-deflection, balanced, traditional, or builder-guided playability. This reduces ambiguity in custom shaft orders and gives unsure customers a safer path to ask for advice.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: Capturing this preference earlier should reduce back-and-forth during quote/spec review, improve perceived expertise, and create a documented reason for build recommendations involving taper, tip diameter, ferrule/endmass choices, and shaft construction.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: The source feedback directly supports adding the field, and billiards physics references confirm deflection/squirt is a meaningful shaft playability attribute. Confidence is below 1.00 because this checkout appears to contain the billiards physics repo and feedback files rather than the production website/order-form implementation.

researchFindings.finding: The raw feedback says, "I like adding the deflection preference," which is a direct positive signal for including the field in the custom ordering experience.

Repository inspection found feedback files and billiards physics code, but no obvious website configurator surface; implementation surface is therefore assumed to be an external/custom order form not present in this checkout.

Dr. Dave Alciatore's "Squirt - Part V: low-squirt cues" defines squirt, also called deflection, as the angular change in initial cue-ball direction from an off-center hit, and explains that lower deflection reduces the amount of aim compensation required when using English.

That same reference notes low-squirt behavior is influenced by shaft-end mass, smaller shaft/tip diameter, ferrule weight, and hollowing or reducing mass near the tip, so the field should feed build/spec review rather than be treated as pure marketing copy.

Technical Proof B.1 relates squirt angle to tip offset and cue effective endmass, and Technical Proof B.19 emphasizes effective endmass as more important than shaft flex for cue-ball deflection, supporting review by a knowledgeable builder before final specs are confirmed.

implementationPlan.step: Add or retain an optional order-form field labeled "Deflection preference" in the shaft playability/spec section, near shaft type, diameter, taper, tip, ferrule, and other playability choices.
Use concise customer-facing helper copy: "How much cue-ball deflection/squirt do you prefer when using side spin? This guides the build review; we will confirm final specs with you."

Offer deterministic options: "Low deflection - less aim adjustment with side spin", "Balanced / medium - familiar all-around response", "Traditional / more deflection - classic response and feedback", "Match my current shaft", and "Not sure - discuss during spec review".

When "Match my current shaft" is selected, prompt for optional supporting notes such as current shaft brand/model, tip diameter, ferrule material, usual bridge length, and what the customer likes or dislikes about the current hit.
Persist the selected value and any supporting note with the order summary, quote request, admin/order detail view, confirmation email, and internal build/spec review checklist.

In the builder review checklist, map the preference to review prompts rather than automatic specs: confirm shaft construction, taper, tip diameter, ferrule/endmass choices, and whether the preference conflicts with other selected options.
Display a short internal warning when a low-deflection preference is paired with specs that may increase endmass or traditional feel, so staff can discuss the tradeoff before accepting the build.
Keep the field optional for checkout completion but visible in admin as "Needs discussion" when the customer selects "Not sure" or leaves a note indicating uncertainty.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: The custom shaft order flow includes a "Deflection preference" field with the five specified options and explanatory helper text.
The field does not claim a guaranteed deflection measurement, exact squirt angle, or objectively superior option.
The selected preference and optional notes appear in customer order review, confirmation records, and staff/admin build review.
Builder/spec review explicitly treats the field as a playability signal used to discuss taper, tip diameter, ferrule/endmass, construction, and tradeoffs.
Selecting "Not sure - discuss during spec review" creates a clear staff follow-up cue without blocking order submission.
Existing orders without a deflection preference remain valid and display the field as blank, not as a defaulted customer choice.

risks.risk: Customers may interpret "low deflection" as universally better; mitigate with neutral wording that presents balanced and traditional response as valid preferences.
Exact deflection depends on multiple specs and manufacturing details; avoid automated promises and route the value through human spec review.
Too many technical terms may overwhelm casual buyers; keep the visible field simple and move details to helper text or staff review.

openQuestions.question: Should the business offer this only on custom/pro shafts, or on every shaft product where construction can materially affect deflection?
Does the builder already classify shafts internally by deflection/playability, and if so what exact internal labels should the admin checklist use?
Should "Match my current shaft" require a current-shaft note before checkout, or remain optional to reduce ordering friction?
